sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in The Colony, TX?
sections.html:
Yes. Owners in The Colony can list with an agent, accept a cash offer, or arrange a quick as-is sale. Because home values here sit well above the Texas norm, the gap between a fast sale and a full-price listing can be larger than in cheaper markets, so compare what you would net on each path.

The Colony is a young city. Its homes were built mostly from the 1970s onward, and several master-planned areas and newer subdivisions compete with resale houses. A seller with a dated interior often faces buyers who compare the house to fresh construction nearby, which is where an as-is cash sale can save the cost of updating.

  • Listing: strongest for a move-in-ready house in a good school zone.
  • Cash sale: strongest when time, repairs or a move date are the main concerns.
  • Rent-out or hold: an option only if the carrying costs work for you.

sections.h2: How did The Colony begin, and why does it matter to sellers?
sections.html:
The city began as a planned community. According to the city's history page, Dallas developer Fox and Jacobs bought about 2,500 acres on the eastern shore of Lake Lewisville in 1973, a municipal utility district was formed for water, and the first families moved in during October 1974.

By January 1977 the community had more than 3,500 residents and voted to incorporate, then became a home rule city in 1979. The name recalls Peters Colony, the settlement contract of the Republic of Texas from 1841 to 1848. Eastvale, a lakeside community begun in the early 1960s, consolidated with the city in 1987, and Lake Lewisville began collecting water in 1954.

For a seller, the age of the neighborhood is the useful part. Houses from the first building wave are now decades old, so roofs, windows and plumbing are the items buyers check first. Newer sections nearer the Grandscape and State Highway 121 area draw different buyers than older lakeside streets.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about The Colony's housing?
sections.html:
QuickFacts puts The Colony at 46,196 residents in July 2025, up 3.7 percent from 2020, a slower pace than neighboring boom towns. The city fits 3,179 people per square mile onto about 14 square miles of land.

sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in The Colony?
sections.html:
Three offices are involved. The city council adopts its own rate during the budget process each September, Denton Central Appraisal District sets the value and grants exemptions, and the Denton County Tax Assessor/Collector bills and collects.

The city's property tax page lists a rate of $.645 per $100 of valuation for fiscal year 2022-2023. That is a past year, so ask the city finance office or the county tax office what the current rate is. The tax is levied on October 1 against the value as of the prior January 1.

  • Denton CAD is at 3911 Morse St. in Denton; the page lists 940-349-3800 and a mailing address of P.O. Box 2816, Denton, TX 76202.
  • The county tax office lists 940-349-3500 in Denton and 940-349-3510 at the Frisco Government Center, 5535 F.M. 423.
  • The city's finance office is at 6053 Main Street and lists 972-624-3140.

On the state side, the Comptroller says taxes unpaid after January 31 turn delinquent on February 1 with a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest. The lien attaches on January 1 and follows the property to a buyer, so the title company pays any balance from your proceeds.

sections.h2: What is the city's homestead exemption in The Colony?
sections.html:
The city says its homestead exemption is 5 percent of the property's market value, and a May 2026 city notice said it had not lowered the percentage. The dollar amount can still change when the market value changes.

That notice explained that appraisal districts must send a notice under Tax Code Section 25.193 whenever an exemption was reduced or cancelled from the prior year. The notice does not by itself mean a taxing unit changed its policy, and an owner should check the exemption code in the table it contains and review status at the Denton CAD website.

  • School districts must give a $140,000 homestead exemption statewide, plus $60,000 more for owners 65 or older and disabled owners.
  • Applications are due by April 30 in most cases.
  • A buyer who moves in after January 1 can claim the exemption for the rest of that year when the prior owner had none.

The city exemption applies only to owners who live in the home, not to rentals or investment property, according to the city's wording in an earlier notice.

sections.h2: What steps and records do I need to sell in The Colony?
sections.html:
The steps run in a set order, whoever the buyer is. First collect your payoff statement, tax bill and any owners' association papers. Then choose a route, sign a contract and open title.

  • Order a payoff from your lender and confirm any lien on record.
  • Pay or arrange taxes through the closing date.
  • Sign the deed before a notary; the county clerk can record it only if it is signed and acknowledged.
  • Have the deed filed in the county where the land sits, which is Denton County for most of The Colony.

A 2023 county clerk manual lists $5.00 for the first page of a recording and $4.00 for each additional page, with added records fees. Ask your title company for the actual figure on your closing statement.

sections.h2: What if the house is inherited, in foreclosure or rented?
sections.html:
Probate generally must be opened within four years of the owner's death, and heirs sometimes use a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit for estates of $75,000 or less excluding the homestead, or a recorded transfer on death deed. Get advice from a Texas probate attorney for your case.

For foreclosure, Texas auctions are held on the first Tuesday of the month after 21 days' notice, and a borrower can reinstate within 20 days of the default notice. A sale before the auction can leave equity in your pocket.

For a rental, the landlord must give written notice to vacate, at least three days unless the lease says otherwise, then file in justice court, where trial is set between 10 and 21 days after filing. A writ of possession can follow six days after final judgment.

faqs.q: Which county is The Colony in for tax and deed purposes?
faqs.a: Denton County, for most of the city. The Denton Central Appraisal District values property and the Denton County tax office collects, with a satellite office in Frisco. Confirm the county on your own tax bill.

faqs.q: Does The Colony have its own homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. The city states its homestead exemption is 5 percent of market value. School districts also give the statewide $140,000 exemption. Apply with Denton CAD by April 30.

faqs.q: Should I update my house before selling in The Colony?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. A cash buyer buys as is. If you list, weigh the cost of updates against the price difference, since buyers often compare your house with newer homes nearby.

faqs.q: How do I find The Colony's current tax rate?
faqs.a: Ask the city finance office or the Denton County tax office. The city's property tax page lists the fiscal year 2022-2023 rate of $.645 per $100, so it should not be used for a current estimate.

faqs.q: Can I sell if I have not paid last year's property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Delinquent taxes with penalty and interest are paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Request a payoff figure good through your closing date.
